question: 3. Apollo Research: (a) Coefficient / Open Philanthropy grants vs the self-reported $1.5M; (b) seed round size and Macroscopic's share; (c) mission board seats
finding: (a) Two archived Open Philanthropy pages give $1,535,480 for startup costs (June 2023) and $2,178,700 general support (May 2024, 'follows our June 2023 support'); the $4,410,180 index total adds a $696,000 May 2026 'staff support' award that exists only in the removed Algolia index, and the Manifund $1.5M self-report equals the first grant alone. (b) Open: no Form D naming Apollo Research in EDGAR full-text search (2025-01-01 to 2026-09-15) and no share allotment at Companies House for Apollo Research AI Ltd (statement of capital GBP 0.01 at incorporation; PSC register says no registrable person); the PBC is a Delaware entity (EIN 93-4310599), which publishes no cap table; the only financing record is a fixed charge to HSBC Innovation Banking registered 9 December 2025. (c) Partial: the PBC post designates the 3rd and 6th board seats as mission seats, says the board currently has 3 seats, and names Daniel Kokotajlo as the first mission director; the other directors are not published (the UK subsidiary's directors are Hobbhahn and, from 15 March 2026, Christopher Akin; Lee Sharkey resigned that day).

question: 7. US CAISI and the EU AI Office: primary-source bounded negatives on lab money
finding: CAISI: the FY2026 Commerce-Justice-Science joint explanatory statement (docs.house.gov, 5 January 2026) provides no less than $55,000,000 for NIST's AI research and measurement science and, within it, up to $10,000,000 to expand NIST's AI efforts through the U.S. Center for AI Standards and Innovation, so the funding is appropriated public money; USAspending's award search returns nothing for 'Center for AI Standards and Innovation', 'CAISI' or 'AI Standards and Innovation' (FY2024 to 2026-09-15, all award types), but USAspending records federal outflows only and cannot show a lab paying NIST, and NIST's published agreement announcements (the August 2024 MOUs with Anthropic and OpenAI) describe an access framework with no payment terms; a NIST CRADA or reimbursable-agreement register was not searchable, so the negative is bounded to those two corpora. EU AI Office: settled, Commission Decision C(2024) 390 Article 8 funds the Office from DG CONNECT staff, Digital Europe Programme administrative appropriations and DEP Specific Objective 2 for operational expenditure, naming no non-Union source.

question: 8. UK AISI: whether Alignment Project funds (including OpenAI money) are administered separately from AISI's evaluation work
finding: AISI's own pages show the pool is not a single AISI-held fund: the Clarification Questions say the funding agreement is between the funder(s) and the host organisation only and funds are paid directly to the host organisation, the How to Apply page says the DSIT/AISI agreement is standard while 'other funders may issue different terms and conditions as part of their GFA', for-profits may receive venture investment rather than grants, and DSIT/AISI's own grants are made under section 5 of the Science and Technology Act 1965 with an 'AISI Research Lead' as grant manager; selection runs through Research Sponsors with a formal assessment panel independent of them. No page states whether the Alignment Project team is organisationally separate from AISI's evaluation teams, so separation from evaluation work is not established.
